data.name: auth.none
data.value: No authentication results (Authentication-Results) in the headers.

data.name: auth.notpass.fix
data.value: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC of the sender, for example with the mail domain check. For external senders this is a warning sign of spoofing.

data.name: bimi.dmarc
data.value: BIMI only works with DMARC p=quarantine or p=reject at pct=100.

data.name: bimi.logo.invalid
data.value: Invalid logo URL ("{0}"). An https address of an .svg file is expected.

data.name: bimi.none.fix
data.value: For a logo in the inbox: "v=BIMI1; l=https://example.com/logo.svg" at default._bimi, logo as SVG Tiny PS.

data.name: bimi.novmc
data.value: No certificate (a=). Gmail and Apple show the logo only with a VMC or CMC.

data.name: cert.csr
data.value: This is a certificate signing request (CSR), not a certificate.

data.name: cert.hint
data.value: One or more certificates with BEGIN CERTIFICATE. Never paste private keys.

data.name: cert.invalid
data.value: The certificate could not be read.

data.name: cert.privatekey
data.value: This is a private key. It was not processed. Never paste private keys into web pages.

data.name: check.Bimi.about
data.value: BIMI shows the brand logo in supporting mailboxes. Requires an enforced DMARC policy.

data.name: check.Dkim.about
data.value: DKIM signs outgoing e-mail. The public key is published at selector._domainkey.domain.

data.name: check.Dmarc.about
data.value: DMARC tells receivers what to do with e-mail that fails SPF and DKIM, and where to send reports.

data.name: check.MtaSts.about
data.value: MTA-STS enforces encrypted delivery (TLS) to the MX servers.

data.name: check.Mx.about
data.value: MX records define which servers accept e-mail for the domain.

data.name: check.Spf.about
data.value: SPF lists the servers allowed to send on behalf of the domain. At most 10 DNS lookups are allowed.

data.name: check.TlsRpt.about
data.value: TLS-RPT delivers reports about problems with encrypted delivery.

data.name: diff.before.hint
data.value: BIND zone file, export of the old provider or lines such as "www CNAME example.com."

data.name: diff.lead
data.value: Compare records from before a migration (zone file or list) with live DNS. Shows missing, changed and new values.

data.name: diff.origin.hint
data.value: Used for relative names such as www or @. A $ORIGIN in the file takes precedence.

data.name: diff.soa
data.value: SOA is skipped because its serial changes with every edit.

data.name: dkim.1024
data.value: DKIM key {0} has {1} bits. Still accepted, 2048 bits are recommended.

data.name: dkim.1024.fix
data.value: Generate a new 2048-bit key and revoke the old one after rotation.

data.name: dkim.invalidkey
data.value: DKIM key {0} cannot be read (p= is not a valid key).

data.name: dkim.invalidkey.fix
data.value: Copy the key again from the mail system. Split long keys into several strings without losing characters.

data.name: dkim.notfound
data.value: No DKIM key found under {0} common selectors.

data.name: dkim.notfound.fix
data.value: Enter the selector from the DKIM-Signature header of a sent mail (s=…) above. If DKIM is missing entirely, enable it at your mail provider.

data.name: dkim.revoked.fix
data.value: Fine if the key was retired on purpose. Otherwise publish a new key.

data.name: dkim.selector.notfound
data.value: There is no DKIM key under selector {0}.

data.name: dkim.selector.notfound.fix
data.value: Check the spelling. The record must be at {0}._domainkey.

data.name: dkim.testing
data.value: DKIM key {0} is in test mode (t=y). Receivers may ignore failures.

data.name: dkim.testing.fix
data.value: Remove t=y once testing is complete.

data.name: dkim.version
data.value: DKIM key {0}: invalid version (v= must be DKIM1).

data.name: dkim.weak
data.value: DKIM key {0} has only {1} bits. This is considered insecure.

data.name: dkim.weak.fix
data.value: Generate a new 2048-bit key and revoke the old one after rotation.

data.name: dmarc.inherited
data.value: No own record. The policy of the organizational domain {0} applies.

data.name: dmarc.multiple
data.value: {0} DMARC records found. Exactly one is allowed, otherwise DMARC is ignored.

data.name: dmarc.none.fix
data.value: Start with monitoring: TXT at _dmarc with "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com". After reviewing reports, raise to quarantine and reject.

data.name: dmarc.p.invalid
data.value: Policy p is missing or invalid ("{0}").

data.name: dmarc.p.none
data.value: Policy p=none: monitoring only, spoofed mail is delivered.

data.name: dmarc.p.none.fix
data.value: Review the reports, then move to p=quarantine and later p=reject.

data.name: dmarc.p.quarantine
data.value: Policy p=quarantine: unauthenticated mail goes to spam.

data.name: dmarc.p.reject
data.value: Policy p=reject: unauthenticated mail is rejected.

data.name: dmarc.pct
data.value: The policy applies to only {0} % of mail (pct).

data.name: dmarc.pct.fix
data.value: Increase pct to 100 step by step or remove it.

data.name: dmarc.rua.invalid
data.value: Invalid report address: {0}. Only mailto: addresses are allowed.

data.name: dmarc.rua.invalid.fix
data.value: Use mailto:address@domain, separate several with commas.

data.name: dmarc.rua.missing
data.value: No report address (rua). Without reports abuse stays invisible.

data.name: dmarc.ruf
data.value: Forensic reports (ruf) requested. Many providers do not send them for privacy reasons.

data.name: dmarc.sp.none
data.value: Subdomains are exempt with sp=none and can be spoofed.

data.name: dmarc.sp.none.fix
data.value: Remove sp (p then applies) or set sp=reject.

data.name: dmarc.strict
data.value: Strict alignment for {0}. Subdomains as senders will then fail DMARC.

data.name: dmarc.syntax.fix
data.value: Format: tag=value separated by semicolons, e.g. "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:…".

data.name: dns.error.fix
data.value: Try again later. If the error persists, check the network or ad blockers.

data.name: enc.binary
data.value: The result is not valid UTF-8 text and is shown as hex.

data.name: enc.invalid
data.value: The input cannot be decoded with this encoding.

data.name: hash.weaknote
data.value: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken. Use them only for checksums of legacy systems, never for passwords or signatures.

data.name: header.dkim.notaligned
data.value: DKIM signature from {0} does not match the sender domain {1}.

data.name: header.dkim.notaligned.fix
data.value: Set up a custom DKIM signature for the sender domain at the sending service so that DMARC passes via DKIM.

data.name: header.empty.fix
data.value: Paste the complete header block, starting with lines such as Received: or From:.

data.name: header.from.displayname
data.value: The display name contains the address {0}, but the mail was sent from {1}.

data.name: header.from.displayname.fix
data.value: Classic deception. Only the address in angle brackets counts.

data.name: header.hint
data.value: Gmail: Show original. Outlook: File, Properties, Internet headers.

data.name: header.lead
data.value: Paste the headers of an e-mail. The analysis shows the route as a timeline, the SPF, DKIM and DMARC results, spam hints and suspicious mismatches.

data.name: header.local
data.value: The analysis runs entirely in the browser. The header is not sent anywhere and not stored.

data.name: header.messageid.domain
data.value: Message-ID comes from {0}, not from the sender domain.

data.name: header.messageid.missing
data.value: No Message-ID. Legitimate mail servers always set one.

data.name: header.replyto.mismatch
data.value: Replies go to {1}, not to the sender domain {0}.

data.name: header.replyto.mismatch.fix
data.value: Typical pattern of phishing and invoice fraud. Verify the address before replying.

data.name: header.returnpath.mismatch
data.value: Sender {0} and Return-Path {1} belong to different domains.

data.name: header.returnpath.mismatch.fix
data.value: Normal for newsletter services. Otherwise a hint of spoofing, especially if DMARC did not pass.

data.name: helpers.lead
data.value: Tools that run completely offline in the browser.

data.name: hop.clockskew
data.value: Hop {0} is earlier than the previous one. A server clock is probably wrong.

data.name: hop.none
data.value: No Received headers found. The route cannot be traced.

data.name: hop.slow.fix
data.value: Common causes: greylisting, queues at the sender or spam filtering.

data.name: jwt.base64
data.value: Invalid Base64url in header or payload.

data.name: jwt.format
data.value: Not a JWT. Three parts separated by dots are expected.

data.name: jwt.hint
data.value: Decoded locally only. The signature is not verified.

data.name: jwt.json
data.value: Header or payload is not a JSON object.

data.name: jwt.jwe
data.value: Encrypted token (JWE). Cannot be read without the key.

data.name: jwt.noverify
data.value: Note: the signature is not verified, that would require the key.

data.name: jwt.status.NotYetValid
data.value: Not yet valid (nbf is in the future).

data.name: jwt.unsigned
data.value: Token is unsigned (alg=none or empty signature). Never trust it.

data.name: mail.invalid
data.value: Please enter a valid domain, for example example.com.

data.name: mail.lead
data.value: Checks MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, MTA-STS and TLS-RPT of a domain and suggests concrete improvements.

data.name: mail.selector.hint
data.value: Found in the DKIM-Signature header after s=. Common selectors are tested automatically.

data.name: mtasts.host.missing
data.value: {0} does not resolve. Without this host the policy cannot be fetched.

data.name: mtasts.host.missing.fix
data.value: Create A/AAAA or a CNAME for the host and serve the policy there over HTTPS.

data.name: mtasts.id.invalid
data.value: Invalid id "{0}" (1 to 32 letters or digits).

data.name: mtasts.id.invalid.fix
data.value: Use e.g. a date such as id=20261121 and change it with every policy update.

data.name: mtasts.multiple
data.value: Multiple MTA-STS records. MTA-STS is then ignored.

data.name: mtasts.none.fix
data.value: Add TXT "v=STSv1; id=20260101" at _mta-sts and serve the policy at https://mta-sts.domain/.well-known/mta-sts.txt.

data.name: mtasts.policy.manual
data.value: The policy file itself cannot be checked from the browser: {0}

data.name: mtasts.policy.manual.fix
data.value: Open the file in the browser and check mode: enforce, mx: and max_age.

data.name: mx.cname
data.value: MX target {0} is a CNAME. RFC 2181 forbids this and some servers reject it.

data.name: mx.cname.fix
data.value: Point the MX directly at the host name that has the A/AAAA record.

data.name: mx.implicit
data.value: No MX record. Senders then deliver to the domain's A record (implicit MX).

data.name: mx.implicit.fix
data.value: Set explicit MX records or publish a null MX "0 ." to state that no mail is accepted.

data.name: mx.ip
data.value: MX record points to an IP address ({0}). MX must point to a host name.

data.name: mx.ip.fix
data.value: Create an A record such as mail.example.com and reference that name in the MX.

data.name: mx.none
data.value: No MX records and no A record: e-mail to this domain cannot be delivered.

data.name: mx.none.fix
data.value: Add the MX records of your mail provider, e.g. "10 mx.example.net.". If the domain should not receive mail, set a null MX "0 .".

data.name: mx.null
data.value: Null MX set: the domain explicitly accepts no e-mail (RFC 7505).

data.name: mx.null.fix
data.value: Pair it with SPF "v=spf1 -all" and DMARC p=reject.

data.name: mx.nxdomain.fix
data.value: Check the spelling or register the domain.

data.name: mx.single
data.value: One MX server found and resolvable.

data.name: mx.single.fix
data.value: For redundancy add a second MX with a higher preference value if your provider offers one.

data.name: mx.unresolvable
data.value: MX target {0} has neither an A nor an AAAA record.

data.name: mx.unresolvable.fix
data.value: Check the MX for typos or add the missing A/AAAA record.

data.name: pw.local
data.value: Generated with cryptographically secure randomness in the browser. Nothing is stored or sent.

data.name: pw.noclass
data.value: Select at least one character class.

data.name: pw.wordlist
data.value: Words from the EFF word list (1296 words, CC BY 3.0).

data.name: spam.clean
data.value: Spam filters did not flag the mail.

data.name: spam.flagged
data.value: At least one spam filter rated the mail as suspicious.

data.name: spf.all.missing
data.value: No "all" at the end. Unlisted servers get a neutral result.

data.name: spf.all.neutral
data.value: ?all is neutral and offers practically no protection.

data.name: spf.all.neutral.fix
data.value: Switch to ~all and, after an observation period, to -all.

data.name: spf.all.notlast
data.value: There are terms after "all". They are never evaluated.

data.name: spf.all.pass
data.value: +all allows every server in the world to send on behalf of the domain.

data.name: spf.all.softfail
data.value: ~all (softfail): unauthorized servers are marked, not rejected. Common together with DMARC.

data.name: spf.include.missing
data.value: Included domain {0} has no SPF record (permerror).

data.name: spf.include.missing.fix
data.value: Remove the include or look up the correct name with the provider.

data.name: spf.lookups.exceeded
data.value: {0} DNS lookups, exceeding the limit of 10. Receivers treat SPF as permerror.

data.name: spf.lookups.exceeded.fix
data.value: Remove unused services, replace ptr/a/mx with ip4/ip6, or move sending services to a subdomain with its own SPF.

data.name: spf.lookups.near
data.value: {0} of 10 DNS lookups used. Any additional service will break the limit.

data.name: spf.lookups.near.fix
data.value: Remove unused includes now or list static networks as ip4/ip6.

data.name: spf.loop.fix
data.value: Remove the include that points back to an already included domain.

data.name: spf.macro
data.value: Macros (%{{…}}) found. They depend on the sender and are not resolved here.

data.name: spf.multiple
data.value: {0} has {1} SPF records. Exactly one is allowed, otherwise SPF fails (permerror).

data.name: spf.multiple.fix
data.value: Merge all entries into a single "v=spf1 …" record.

data.name: spf.none.fix
data.value: Add a TXT record at the domain, e.g. "v=spf1 mx -all" or with your mail provider's include. If the domain never sends mail: "v=spf1 -all".

data.name: spf.ptr
data.value: The ptr mechanism is deprecated (RFC 7208), slow and unreliable.

data.name: spf.ptr.fix
data.value: Replace ptr with ip4/ip6 or a.

data.name: spf.redirect.ignored
data.value: redirect= is ignored because the record contains "all".

data.name: spf.redirect.ignored.fix
data.value: Use either redirect= or all, not both.

data.name: spf.syntax.fix
data.value: Check the syntax. Valid examples: ip4:192.0.2.0/24, include:_spf.example.net, mx, -all.

data.name: spf.toodeep
data.value: More than {0} nested SPF records, evaluation stopped.

data.name: spf.toodeep.fix
data.value: Reduce the includes, see the lookup limit.

data.name: spf.voidlookups
data.value: {0} lookups without a result (limit 2). Receivers may treat SPF as permerror.

data.name: spf.voidlookups.fix
data.value: Remove references to domains and hosts that do not exist.

data.name: subnet.contains
data.value: Is an IP in the network?

data.name: subnet.invalid
data.value: Invalid input. An IP with optional prefix length or netmask is expected.

data.name: subnet.lead
data.value: IPv4 and IPv6: network, broadcast, host range, splitting into subnets, summarizing and checking whether an IP is in the network.

data.name: subnet.p2p
data.value: /31 and /32 have no network or broadcast address (RFC 3021), all addresses are usable.

data.name: subnet.split.range
data.value: Enter a prefix length between {0} and {1}.

data.name: subnet.summarize.lead
data.value: Combines networks and addresses into the smallest list of CIDR blocks that covers exactly the same addresses.

data.name: tlsrpt.none.sts
data.value: MTA-STS is active but TLS-RPT is missing. Delivery problems go unnoticed.

data.name: tlsrpt.rua.invalid
data.value: Invalid report address "{0}". mailto: and https: are allowed.

data.name: ui.dnsnotice
data.value: Your input stays in the browser. Only DNS queries are sent, encrypted, to Cloudflare DNS (fallback: Google Public DNS).

data.name: zone.owner
data.value: Line starts with whitespace but there is no previous name: {0}

data.name: zone.toomany
